g4-order-01.notes: d = leftmost usable non-c1 cell; s = nearest c1 to its right. Sum of c1 positions strictly falls; when no c1 lies right of d, every c1 sits left of d and no c2 does, so ORDER holds. Swap spare exists whenever any move is possible.

g4-order-02.notes: Leftmost c2 as target; the first c1 to its right swaps in. Exists exactly when ORDER fails.

g4-order-03.notes: d = leftmost movable non-c1 object (empties skipped). Same termination argument as packing c1 left of the first c2.

g4-order-04.notes: Fills the leftmost usable c1-length window. Correct without obstacles; with obstacles a c2 can sit in the fragment left of G1, and once G1 is full nothing moves.

g4-order-05.notes: Only an immediately adjacent c1 can be used; when the nearest c1 right of d is 2+ cells away nothing moves.

g4-order-06.notes: Ignores PARTNER cells as targets. e.g. [c2,c1,_]: d is the empty cell, no c1 to its right -> stuck.

g4-order-07.notes: Nested AND that reduces to RIGHT_OF_DEST (tests two-level nesting). Same argument as the PARTNER/EMPTY design.

g4-order-08.notes: d = leftmost c2 or droppable empty; OTHER objects are skipped. If no c1 right of d then all c1 precede the first c2.

g4-order-09.notes: Leftmost usable non-c1 cell receives the globally rightmost c1. If that c1 were left of d all c1 would be packed left and ORDER would already hold, so the move is always leftward.

g4-order-10.notes: Without obstacles G1=[0,c) and a c1 outside the window right of the leftmost c2 always exists. With hazards (NO_DROP_HAZARD) or NO_PICK objects near the left edge, G1 shifts right and the only c1 right of d can lie inside G1 -> no move while ORDER fails.

g4-order-11.notes: Nearest c1 may be left of the leftmost c2 and gets pushed right. e.g. [c1,c2,c1,_] oscillates forever.

g4-order-12.notes: Swap the rightmost c1 with the leftmost c2. Not holding <=> rightmost c1 is right of leftmost c2, so a move always exists and moves c1 leftward; each swap permanently fixes one c1 left of the remaining c2 front.

g4-order-13.notes: Leftmost movable non-c1 object swapped with the farthest c1 to its right.

g4-order-14.notes: Variant of the rightmost-c1 swap using any movable non-c1 object as target; d is at or before the leftmost c2.

g4-order-15.notes: Leftmost c2 swapped with the closest c1 to its right; adjacent-transposition flavour, still monotone.

g4-zone-01.notes: Mirror of left packing for right zones.

g4-zone-02.notes: Right packing with the closest c on the left (rightmost of LEFT_OF_DEST).

g4-zone-03.notes: For a right zone everything outside the zone is left of any zone cell, so the AND equals NOT_ZONE.

g4-zone-04.notes: Same monotone fill of the zone with different picks.

g4-zone-05.notes: d is the leftmost usable non-c cell; if it were outside the zone, the zone's usable cells would all be c and the atom would hold. So d is in the zone and every c outside is to its right.

g4-zone-06.notes: Without obstacles G1=[0,c) lies inside a feasible left zone. With hazards/NO_PICK objects inside the zone, the usable zone cells may be non-contiguous and G1 extends past the zone -> fills G1 and stops short of the atom.

g4-zone-07.notes: Zone-agnostic left packing: c objects end on the first count usable cells, which feasibility puts inside the left zone. Each move fixes one c permanently.

g4-zone-08.notes: For a left zone everything outside the zone is right of any zone cell, so the AND equals NOT_ZONE.

g4-zone-09.notes: Same monotone fill of the zone with different picks.

g4-zone-10.notes: Needs at least two usable non-c cells in the zone; the last step (one free slot left) never happens.

g4-zone-11.notes: Source may already be inside the zone (shuffling, oscillation) and c objects farther than 2 cells are invisible.

g4-zone-12.notes: Only empties as targets: other-coloured objects occupying the zone are never displaced. e.g. [x,x,c,_] with w=2.

g4-zone-13.notes: Left packing pulling the farthest c.

g4-zone-14.notes: Nested AND in the destination that reduces to ZONE (tests two-level nesting in dest).

g4-zone-15.notes: Each move brings one more c into the zone onto a usable non-c cell; feasibility (c count <= usable zone cells) guarantees such a cell while some c is outside.

g4-group-05.notes: AND / nested AND that reduce to the plain G1 fill.

g4-group-06.notes: Ignores c objects left of G1. Without obstacles G1 starts at 0 so none exist; with obstacles a c stranded in the fragment left of G1 is never fetched.

g4-group-09.notes: Packs c onto the leftmost usable cells. Contiguous without obstacles; with a hazard (NO_DROP_HAZARD) or NO_PICK object among those cells it terminates non-contiguous.

g4-group-10.notes: Window is fixed (depends only on count, hazards, NO_PICK objects). Each move adds one c to G1; when G1 is all c, the c objects are contiguous. Any feasible instance has a usable window.

g4-group-12.notes: Needs two c objects outside G2; the last c is never brought in.

g4-group-13.notes: c objects more than 3 cells from the target are invisible -> stuck on spread-out instances.

g4-group-15.notes: Only other-coloured objects as targets: window cells that are simply empty are never filled.
